question: Who was the last Jain Tirthankara?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahavira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahavira, also known as Vardhamana, is recognized as the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism.
 
• He was born in 599 BCE in the kingdom of Vaishali, now in Bihar, India.
 
• Mahavira attained Kevala Jnana (omniscience) after 12 years of rigorous ascetic practices.
 
• He preached the principles of Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (chastity), and Aparigraha (non-possessiveness).
 
• Mahavira's teachings form the foundation of Jain philosophy and are compiled in the Jain Agamas, the canonical scriptures of Jainism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jain Tirthankaras**

 
 
• Tirthankaras are spiritual teachers in Jainism who have conquered the cycle of birth and death and attained liberation (Moksha).
 
• There are 24 Tirthankaras in Jain tradition, with Rishabhanatha being the first and Mahavira the last.
 
• Each Tirthankara revitalizes the Jain community and re-establishes the fourfold order of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen.
 
 
 
• **Jainism**
 
 
• Jainism is one of the oldest religions in the world, originating in India around the 6th century BCE.
 
• It emphasizes non-violence, truth, and asceticism as a means to attain spiritual liberation.
 
• Jains practice strict vegetarianism and often engage in fasting and other forms of self-discipline to purify the soul.
 
 
 
• **Kevala Jnana**
 
 
• Kevala Jnana, or omniscience, is the highest form of knowledge in Jainism, attained by a Tirthankara.
 
• It signifies the complete understanding of the universe, free from all forms of karma.
 
• An individual with Kevala Jnana can see past, present, and future events simultaneously.
 
 
 
• **Jain Agamas**
 
 
• The Jain Agamas are the canonical scriptures of Jainism, originally composed in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit.
 
• They consist of teachings attributed to the Tirthankaras, primarily Mahavira.
 
• The Agamas are divided into two main sects: Svetambara and Digambara, with slight variations in their texts.
